message.content:
Add **dual-mode** to Build Studio in the Nxeon customer portal (/opt/nxeon, Next.js App Router + React). Today Build Studio hard-requires an Anthropic API key. The owner wants **two ways to build, chosen per console**:

1. **"Use my Anthropic key"** — the EXISTING flow (plan-then-approve via the platform calling the Anthropic API with the customer's BYOK key). Keep it exactly as-is.
2. **"Use Claude on my server"** (NEW, no API key needed) — open a **real web terminal** into the chosen RUNNING server, where the `claude` CLI is now pre-installed (`/usr/local/bin/claude`). The customer runs `claude` there authenticated with their **own Claude Pro/Max subscription** (or a key they set on the server). Zero platform API cost.

## Reuse (do NOT reinvent — the terminal + auth already exist)
- `components/customer/WebTerminal.tsx` — an **embeddable xterm.js terminal**. It mints a short-lived, ownership-checked token via `POST /api/terminal/token` ({serverId}) and connects a WebSocket to `/terminal-ws?token=...`. It never sees server credentials. READ it to learn its props (`servers: {id,hostname}[]`, `serverId` state, etc.) and how to embed it. This is the terminal for mode 2 — one per console, targeting that console's selected server.
- `components/customer/terminal/TerminalDock.tsx` (`useTerminalDock`/`TerminalDockProvider`, already mounted in `components/portal/Shell.tsx`) — an alternative if a provider-based session fits better. Prefer embedding `WebTerminal` inline in the console pane so each console has its own terminal.
- Existing API-key path: `lib/actions-claude-console.ts` (`planConsoleBuild`/`listConsoleBuilds`), `components/customer/claude-code/BuildConsole.tsx`, `approveBuild`/`rejectBuild`. Leave this path intact.

## What to change
- **`app/dashboard/build/page.tsx`** — REMOVE the hard `usable = keyConnected || platformKeyConfigured()` gate (line ~41) that blocks the whole page. Render Build Studio regardless of key state; pass `keyConnected` (Boolean(anthropicKeyEnc) || platformKeyConfigured) down to BuildStudio. Keep the "no RUNNING servers" empty state — BOTH modes need a running server (mode 1 SSH-executes onto it, mode 2 terminals into it). The "Add your API key" card should now be **contextual to mode 1 only**, not a full-page block.
- **`components/customer/claude-code/BuildStudio.tsx` + `BuildConsole.tsx`** — each console gets a **mode toggle** ("Use my Anthropic key" | "Use Claude on my server"). Default to server-terminal mode when no key is connected, API-key mode when a key exists. In server-terminal mode the console body renders `<WebTerminal servers={[selectedServer]} />` (or the dock session) targeting that console's picked server, with a one-line hint: "Run `claude` to start — sign in with your Claude subscription or API key." In API-key mode, render the existing plan/approve console; if `!keyConnected`, show the "Add your API key" prompt inside that mode only (link to `/dashboard/settings?tab=integrations#anthropic-key`). Multi-console (1–6), per-console server picker, mirror mode, and the Pipeline Board all stay.

## Platform rules (non-negotiable)
- `/api/terminal/token` already enforces session + server ownership; don't weaken it. The terminal must only ever target a RUNNING server the customer owns.
- Don't break the existing API-key path, its tests, or the `planConsoleBuild`/approve safety flow.
- Copy must be honest: server-terminal mode does NOT run through the platform's plan-then-approve gate (the customer is driving `claude` directly on their own box) — say so plainly; don't imply the platform is reviewing those commands.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for your files. Tests via `npm test` (node:test). Add tests that bite: the page no longer hard-blocks without a key (source tripwire via `stripCommentsAndStrings` from `test/_source-tools.ts` that the `usable`-gate early-return is gone and BuildStudio renders), the mode toggle exists, and server-terminal mode routes through WebTerminal/token (not a fake). Reuse existing Build Studio tests; don't regress them.
- Do NOT run prisma db push, next build in place, git commit, deploy, or systemctl. I integrate centrally.

## Deliver
Typechecking code + tests. Final report: files changed, how the mode toggle + default works, exactly how server-terminal mode embeds the terminal (which component, how the selected server flows in), what you changed in page.tsx's gate, test count, and anything you simulated vs really wired. Report is data for me, not a user message.

content.text:
Done. All changes complete, full typecheck clean, and all 748 tests pass (24 in the Matrix/Build Studio suite, 7 newly added).

## Files changed

- **`app/dashboard/build/page.tsx`** — removed the `usable` gate.
- **`components/customer/claude-code/BuildStudio.tsx`** — accepts/threads `keyConnected`, computes per-console `initialMode`, renamed to Matrix.
- **`components/customer/claude-code/BuildConsole.tsx`** — added mode toggle + server-terminal body.
- **`components/customer/WebTerminal.tsx`** — added inline `embedded` mode + optional `hint`.
- **`test/build-studio.test.ts`** — 7 new tripwire tests.

## How the mode toggle + default works
Each `BuildConsole` holds `mode` state (`"key" | "server"`), seeded from an `initialMode` prop. BuildStudio computes it per console: `c.autoPrompt ? "key" : keyConnected ? "key" : "server"` — so a console defaults to **server-terminal mode when no key is connected**, **API-key mode when a key exists**, and mirror-launched consoles (which carry an `autoPrompt` for the plan/approve flow) always start in key mode. A two-button segmented control in each console header lets the user switch modes live; the phase badge shows only in key mode (a plain "terminal" badge shows in server mode).

## How server-terminal mode embeds the terminal
In server mode the console body renders the real `<WebTerminal>` inline. I extended WebTerminal with an `embedded` prop: when set it renders inline filling the console pane (no portal/backdrop, `onClose` now optional) instead of its full-screen slide-in — that component was used nowhere else, so this is safe. The console passes `servers={[server]}` where `server` is the console's currently-selected server (from the existing per-console header picker), plus `key={server.id}` so switching the picker cleanly remounts the terminal onto the new box. WebTerminal is unchanged in how it authorizes: it still `POST`s `/api/terminal/token` (session + ownership checked) and opens the `/terminal-ws` PTY WebSocket — so mode 2 routes through the real, ownership-enforced path, never a stub. A one-line hint above the terminal tells the user to run `claude` and states plainly that these commands run straight on their server and Nxeon does not review them (no plan-then-approve).

If a console is in key mode but `!keyConnected`, the body shows a contextual "Add your API key" card (linking to `/dashboard/settings?tab=integrations#anthropic-key`) with a pointer to switch to server mode — scoped to that mode only, not a full-page block.

## page.tsx gate change
Deleted the `usable` variable and the entire `if (!usable) { ... }` full-page block. `keyConnected` is now `Boolean(anthropicKeyEnc) || platformKeyConfigured()` and is passed down to `BuildStudio` rather than used to block. The "No running servers" empty state is kept (both modes need a running server). `BuildStudio` now renders unconditionally when at least one running server exists.

## Tests (7 new, 24 total in suite)
1. Page no longer hard-blocks: `usable` var + `if (!usable)` early-return gone; `<BuildStudio>` rendered with `keyConnected` (shape tripwire via `stripCommentsAndStrings`).
2. Empty state retained (`servers.length === 0` + "No running servers" copy).
3. Mode toggle present — both mode labels + `setMode`/`mode ===` branching.
4. BuildStudio threads `keyConnected` and derives `initialMode`.
5. Server-terminal mode routes through the **real** WebTerminal + `/api/terminal/token` + `/terminal-ws` + real `fetch`/`new WebSocket` (proves it's not a fake).
6. Honest copy: platform does not review terminal commands.

## Matrix rename (per your mid-task instruction)
Renamed in my owned files: `WORKSPACE_NAME` → `"Matrix"` (BuildStudio.tsx), page `metadata.title` and both empty-state PageHeader titles → "Matrix" (page.tsx), updated the BuildStudio sub/description to the honest dual-mode wording, and cleaned two internal doc comments.

**Stray "Build Studio" references remaining** (outside my owned files, both are non-user-visible code comments — flagging for you to sweep centrally):
- `lib/claude-console-core.ts:1`
- `lib/actions-claude-console.ts:3`

## Simulated vs really wired
Everything is really wired — no stubs. The only thing I did not exercise is a live WebSocket handshake against a running server (no runtime env here); that path is unchanged from the existing, already-deployed WebTerminal token/PTY flow, and the tests assert the wiring statically. I did not run `prisma db push`, `next build`, `git commit`, deploy, or `systemctl`.
